key_insight: The paper shows that a small set of human-style visual cues can drive most social bias judgments in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). By isolating appearance from identity, it reveals which attributes actually trigger biased responses.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of separating true appearance-based bias from confounding identity differences in prior bias studies. The paper provides a controlled way to measure attribute-level social bias in MLLMs using standardized face variations.
method: Created StylisticBias, a controlled benchmark built from 500 photorealistic base faces.
Systematically edited visual attributes on the same identities to isolate the effect of specific cues.
Evaluated MLLMs on bias-related judgments to identify which human visual features most influence model behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this helps reveal hidden bias mechanisms in multimodal systems before deployment in high-stakes settings. It also offers a more rigorous benchmark for auditing fairness in models that interpret people from images.

paper_title: StylisticBias: A Few Human Visual Cues Drive Most Social Biases in MLLMs
